repurposing_rationale.mechanistic_link: 無直接機轉關聯。此為自體免疫性神經疾病（局部型 stiff person spectrum disorder），以 anti-GAD 抗體及 GABA 缺乏介導局部肌肉僵硬為特徵。TxGNN 可能透過代謝-免疫知識圖譜網路節點偵測遠端連結（如腸道微生物菌群→腸-腦軸→GABAergic 系統），但此推測路徑缺乏任何實驗或臨床支持。

與 focal 型同屬 stiff person spectrum disorder，以高效價 anti-GAD65 抗體為特徵，主要機轉為中樞 GABAergic 抑制神經元受損。Acarbose 的代謝調節作用（餐後血糖、腸道菌群）對此疾病的病理核心（自體免疫 GABA 缺乏）無已知干預路徑。評分與 focal 型完全相同（0.9965）提示 KG 模型可能存在共享節點評分現象，不代表額外生物學證據。
由 SLC19A2（ThTr1 硫胺素轉運蛋白）突變引起的罕見常染色體隱性遺傳病，表現為糖尿病、巨球性貧血及感音神經性耳聾三聯症。其糖尿病成分為胰島素分泌缺乏，補充硫胺素可部分恢復 β 細胞功能。Acarbose 雖可理論上減少餐後葡萄糖毒性，但硫胺素補充為核心治療，Acarbose 的輔助角色純屬推測，且無任何案例報告或試驗支持。

由 INPPL1（編碼 SHIP2：SH2 domain-containing inositol 5-phosphatase 2）功能喪失突變引起的超罕見骨骼發育異常（<50 例全球報告）。SHIP2 參與 PI3K/Akt 胰島素訊號下游調控，這是 TxGNN 可能偵測到此關聯的理論路徑，但 opsismodysplasia 的臨床問題為骨骼礦化缺陷而非代謝失調。Acarbose 對此病的潛在影響在概念上極遠，無任何臨床轉化意義。
最常見形式為胰島素注射部位脂肪萎縮或脂肪增生（lipohypertrophy）。理論連結：Acarbose 改善餐後血糖控制 → 減少所需胰島素劑量 → 減少注射頻率 → 減少局部組織損傷。然而此推理鏈條過長且缺乏臨床驗證；更有效的干預為輪換注射部位與使用純化胰島素製劑。
向心性脂肪萎縮症（Lipodystrophia centrifugalis abdominalis infantilis）為兒童罕見脂肪萎縮症，病因涉及局部炎症與脂肪組織代謝異常，與胰島素代謝的關聯極為間接。TxGNN 可能透過脂肪代謝知識圖譜節點偵測此關聯，無任何已知生物學路徑或臨床報告支持 Acarbose 的應用。
由持續性機械壓力（如輪椅坐墊、義肢接觸面）引起的局部脂肪組織萎縮，為物理性損傷機轉主導。Acarbose 的代謝作用機制與此物理性疾病無合理交集。此預測可能反映 KG 中「脂肪組織異常」類別節點的廣泛連結，而非真實生物學關聯。
病因未明的局部脂肪萎縮，可能與局部炎症、外傷或特發性脂肪細胞凋亡相關。部分研究顯示局部胰島素抵抗可能參與脂肪組織異常，Acarbose 改善全身胰島素敏感性的間接效應在理論層面有極遠關聯，但無法構成推薦依據。

clinical_trials.title: A Randomized, Double-Blind Trial Comparing the Effect of the Addition of Dulaglutide 1.5 mg Versus the Addition of Placebo to Titrated Basal Insulin on Glycemic Control in Chinese Patients With Type 2 Diabetes
clinical_trials.brief_summary: The main purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety and efficacy of once weekly dulaglutide when added to insulin glargine, with metformin and/or acarbose in Chinese participants with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

clinical_trials.title: The Effect of Vildagliptin on Endothelium-dependent Vasodilatation. A Double Blind Cross-over Study in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
clinical_trials.brief_summary:

clinical_trials.title: High-amylose Barley (HIAMBA) in the Regulation and Prevention of Type 2 Diabetes: a Randomized, Cross-over, Acute Dietary Intervention Study.
clinical_trials.brief_summary: In a series of double-blinded randomized cross-over acute studies, the investigators want to study the effects of naturally produced high-amylose barley (Lean-baking barley®) on the postprandial glucose-metabolism in subjects with and without type 2 diabetes (T2D).

clinical_trials.title: Glucobay M - Evaluation of Safety and Effectiveness in Type 2 Diabetes Not Well Controlled on Monotherapy in Real Life Practice
clinical_trials.brief_summary: The study is designed as non interventional to collect data on the safety especially, severe hypoglycemia or documented symptomatic hypoglycemic episodes and effectiveness of acarbose/metformin fixed-dose combination under real-life treatment condition in large sample of type-2 diabetes patients in India. clinical_trials.title: Effect of Low Glycemic Index Diets on Glucose Control in Non-Insulin Dependent Diabetics
clinical_trials.brief_summary: Large observational studies have shown cereal fiber to protect from diabetes and heart disease. Despite the success of acarbose, an α-glucosidase hydrolase inhibitor, which lowers the glycemic index of foods containing starch, sucrose and maltodextrins, the use of diets containing low glycemic index foods still remains to be established. clinical_trials.title: Effect of Acarbose and Fixed Mixture of Pioglitazone and Metformin in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Receiving Anti-diabetic Monotherapy
clinical_trials.brief_summary: Monotherapy with DPP-IV inhibitors, SGLT-2 inhibitors or insulin secretagogues frequently failed to maintain blood glucose in patients with type 2 diabtes. It was critical to determine which was more suitable of acarbose versus metformin plus pioglitazone.

clinical_trials.title: Efficacy and Safety of Omarigliptin, A Weekly Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 Inhibitor for Type 2 Diabetes Management: Real-World Evaluation in Bangladesh
clinical_trials.brief_summary: The study titled "Efficacy and Safety of Omarigliptin, A Weekly Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 Inhibitor for Type 2 Diabetes Management: Real-World Evaluation in Bangladesh" aims to assess the real-world effectiveness and safety of omarigliptin in managing newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) patients. Conducted at BIRDEM General Hospital, this 12-month observational study involves 938 patients aged 18 years or older, newly diagnosed with T2DM, with no prior use of antidiabetic medications.

clinical_trials.title: Comparison of Canagliflozin vs. Alternative Antihyperglycemic Treatments on Risk of Heart Failure Hospitalization and Amputation for Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and the Subpopulation With Established Cardiovascular Disease
clinical_trials.brief_summary: The primary purpose of study is to estimate the incidence and comparative effect on health outcomes: 1) hospitalization for heart failure, 2) below knee lower extremity amputation. The date of first exposure to the particular drug(s) in the database, where the exposure start is between 1-April-2013 to 15-May-2017 and outcome data for these participants will be analyzed and reported in this study.

clinical_trials.title: Effectiveness and Safety of Glucose-lowering Drugs as an Adjunct to Insulin Therapy in Chinese Patients With Type 1 Diabetes: a Retrospective, Observational Study
clinical_trials.brief_summary:
To assess the real-world impact of glucose-lowering drugs (GLDs) as an adjunct to insulin in Chinese patients with type 1 diabetes (T1DM).

Does glucose-lowering drugs (GLDs) as an adjunct to insulin improve clinical outcomes in Chinese patients with type 1 diabetes (T1DM) when used long-term in real-world practice?

clinical_trials.title: A Randomized, Open-label, Non-inferiority Study to Compare the Efficacy and Safety of Voglibose and Acarbose in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus With Poor Control of Metformin
clinical_trials.brief_summary: The primary purpose of this study is to evaluate the efficacy of voglibose versus acarbose combined with metformin in participants with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) by evaluating levels of glycosylated hemoglobin.

clinical_trials.title: Response of Gut Microbiota in Type 2 Diabetes to Hypoglycemic Agents
clinical_trials.brief_summary: Intestinal microflora refers to the trillions of microorganisms living in our gut, which is considered as an independent endocrine organ of human body. Intestinal microbiota plays a very important role in human health. The composition of human intestinal microbiota is affected by a variety of factors, including age, living region, eating habits, nutrition, probiotics, antibiotics and so on. clinical_trials.title: Remission Evaluation of Metabolic Interventions in Type 2 Diabetes (REMIT): A Randomized Controlled Pilot Trial
clinical_trials.brief_summary: The purpose of this pilot trial is to determine whether an intensive treatment with insulin glargine, metformin, acarbose and lifestyle can normalize blood glucose levels in patients with recently diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus when compared to standard diabetes care.

clinical_trials.title: Metabolic Syndrome and Its Single Traits as Risk Factors of Diabetes in People With Impaired Glucose Tolerance: The STOP-NIDDM Trial
clinical_trials.brief_summary:
The aim of the study was to analyse the independent and joint effects of the components of the metabolic syndrome (MetS) on the incidence of diabetes in people with impaired glucose tolerance (IGT) and to assess the effect of acarbose by MetS status.

Double-blind placebo controlled trial, 1,368 patients, follow-up time 3.3 years. MetS by ATP III definition with fasting plasma glucose of ≥ 6.1 mmol/l as limit for impaired fasting glucose (IFG).

clinical_trials.title: Randomized, Non-blinded, 3-fold Crossover Study to Investigate the Bioequivalence Between Glucobay ODT 100 mg Taken Without and With Water and the Glucobay Standard Tablet 100 mg Following Single Oral Dosing in Healthy Male Subjects
clinical_trials.brief_summary: To establish the bioequivalence between Glucobay ODT (Orally Disintegrating Tablet) 100 mg taken without or with water and the Glucobay standard tablet 100 mg taken with water.

clinical_trials.title: Non-inferiority Between Acarbose and Prandial Insulin for the Treatment of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: a Randomized Multicenter and Prospective Trial. ACARB-GDM Study.
clinical_trials.brief_summary: Caring for women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is very time-consuming. Therapeutic strategy includes dietary and lifestyle measures and additional insulin therapy for 15 to 40% of the women with GDM if the glycemic targets are not achieved after a period of 1 to 2 weeks of diet. Insulin therapy is imperfect for the following main reasons: need for education (i.e. subcutaneous administration, dose titration), hypoglycemia and weight gain, limited acceptance and high cost. clinical_trials.title: A Randomized, Non-inferiority, Open-label Clinical Trial to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of GAcarbose+Saxagliptin Compared With Metformin+Saxagliptin in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes in Chinese
clinical_trials.brief_summary: To investigate the Safety and Efficacy of Acarbose+Saxagliptin Compared With Metformin+Saxagliptin in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes,100 patients with T2DM will be enrolled in this study.They will randomly be assigned to Acarbose+Saxagliptin or Metformin+Saxagliptin group.HbA1c，fasting and postprandial C-peptide will be observed before and after the interventions.

clinical_trials.title: A Multicentre Observational Study to Investigate the Improvement in Glucose FLuctuation of Sufficient Acarbose Therapy on Type 2 Diabetes Patient With High Blood Glucose Fluctuation
clinical_trials.brief_summary: This is a multicentre observational study to investigate the improvement in glucose fluctuation of sufficient acarbose therapy on type 2 diabetes patient with high blood glucose fluctuation

clinical_trials.title: SMART Study - A 24-Week, Multicenter, Randomized, Parallel-group, Open-label, Active Controlled Phase IV Study to Assess the Efficacy, Safety and Tolerability of Saxagliptin Compared With Acarbose When in Combination With Metformin in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2D) Inadequately Controlled With Metformin Monotherapy
clinical_trials.brief_summary: SMART Study - A 24-Week, Multicenter, Randomized, Parallel-group, Open-label, Active Controlled Phase IV Study to Assess the Efficacy, Safety and Tolerability of Saxagliptin Compared with Acarbose when in Combination with Metformin in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2D) Inadequately Controlled with Metformin Monotherapy

clinical_trials.title: Comparison of Diabetes Retinopathy Among Type 2 Diabetic Patients Treated With Different Regimens: a Multicentre Randomized Parallel-group Clinical Trial
clinical_trials.brief_summary: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is an important cause of blindness.

clinical_trials.title: The Effects of Saxagliptin 5mg, Once Daily for 52 Weeks on 24 Hour Urine Albumin Creatinine Rate(ACR) , in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Who Have Inadequate Glycaemic Control on Metformin or/and Acarbose
clinical_trials.brief_summary: This study compare the effects on microalbuminuria improvement in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) treated with saxagliptin or glimepiride.All patients received metformin and/or acarbose, and randomly receive saxagliptin (5mg/d) or glimepiride (1-4mg/d).

clinical_trials.title: Multicomponent Intervention on Lifestyle, Anthropometric Measurements, Glycemic Control and Quality of Life in Patients Obese People With Type II Diabetes
clinical_trials.brief_summary: The main objective of this study will be to evaluate the effectiveness of a multicomponent intervention on nutritional recommendations and physical activity on glycemic control in obese patients with Type II Diabetes (DM2) in three places at the Algodonera Health Center of the Care Management Integrated in Talavera de la Reina.

literature.title: Comparison of adjunctive therapy with metformin and acarbose in patients with Type-1 diabetes mellitus.
literature.abstract: All the aforementioned data have stimulated interest in studying other potential therapies for T1DM including noninsulin pharmacological therapies. The present study attempts to investigate the effect of adjunctive therapy with metformin and acarbose in patients with Type-1 diabetes mellitus.

literature.abstract: The aim of the study was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of acarbose in patients with Type 1 diabetes mellitus (DM).

literature.title: Effects of the addition of acarbose to insulin and non-insulin regimens in veterans with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
literature.abstract: The primary objective of the study was to assess the mean change in hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) when acarbose was added to insulin and non-insulin regimens in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Secondary objectives were to evaluate the discontinuation rate of acarbose, and to assess the number of patients who were placed on insulin despite the addition of acarbose.

The valid-case population was 15. All patients were well controlled on insulin therapy and diet. literature.title: Acarbose in the treatment of type I diabetes.
literature.abstract: This 36-week multicenter double-blind placebo-controlled study was designed to assess the safety and efficacy of acarbose, administered in conjunction with diet and insulin therapy, for the treatment of patients with type I diabetes.

literature.title: Comparative efficacy and safety of glucose-lowering drugs as adjunctive therapy for adults with type 1 diabetes: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
literature.abstract: To assess the efficacy and safety of glucose-lowering drugs used as an adjunct to insulin therapy in adults with type 1 diabetes.

literature.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
literature.abstract: We assessed four putative bedtime treatments in the prevention of nocturnal hypoglycemia in type 1 diabetes.

literature.abstract: The primary objective of this double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised cross-over study was to investigate the influence of acarbose on insulin requirement in patients with Type 1 diabetes (T1DM) following a standardised meal. In addition, the study assessed the effects of acarbose on post-prandial triglyceride, glucagon and gastrointestinal peptide levels, gastric emptying, and oxidative glucose metabolism. literature.title: Postprandial hypotension treated with acarbose in a patient with type 1 diabetes mellitus.
literature.journal: Clinical autonomic research : official journal of the Clinical Autonomic Research Society
literature.abstract: Treatment of postprandial hypotension (PPH) is often unsuccessful. We report a case of a type 1 diabetic patient suffering from severely symptomatic PPH. The patient was treated with acarbose and showed definite improvement of both glycemic control and PPH.

repurposing_rationale.mechanistic_link: 最強機轉連結。T1DM 患者依賴外源性胰島素，但餐後血糖尖峰控制仍困難（快速胰島素動力學滯後於葡萄糖吸收）。Acarbose 介入機制：(1) 延緩小腸碳水化合物分解吸收 → 減少餐後血糖峰值 ΔHbA1c ~0.3-0.5%；(2) 允許縮短或消除胰島素注射-進食等待時間；(3) 減少餐後低血糖反應性風險；(4) 可能在新診斷 T1DM 中透過降低葡萄糖毒性，間接保護殘存 β 細胞功能（honeymoon phase）。多項 RCT 已在 T1DM 族群中驗證此輔助療法，系統性回顧確認整體安全性與中度療效。主要限制：GI 副作用（脹氣 15-35%、腹瀉）在嚴格碳水化合物飲食控制的 T1DM 患者中可能影響依從性；需監控低血糖處置（此時應使用葡萄糖而非蔗糖）。
